findings.reason: Compose.razor SwitchToRichTextAsync passes the output of markedInterop.toHtml (marked.parse with no sanitizer) to quillInterop.setHtml, which sets root.innerHTML directly. auth.js:5-6 keeps both tokens in localStorage, so an img onerror payload could read them. Lowered from high because the user has to paste the attacker's Markdown into their own editor (self-XSS); nothing in this change loads outside content into it.
findings.claim: Switching Markdown to rich text runs any HTML in the Markdown without sanitizing it, so script in that content executes in the logged-in app.
findings.evidence: Compose.SwitchToRichTextAsync passes markedInterop.toHtml output directly to setHtml, which assigns root.innerHTML without sanitizing it. Pasting `` into Markdown and switching modes reaches this sink. [Marked explicitly preserves unsafe HTML](https://marked.js.org/#usage). The outgoing server sanitizer runs only during sending; auth.js stores both authentication tokens in localStorage.

findings.reason: getHtml returns Quill's internal root.innerHTML. Quill 2.0.3 (index.html loads that version) writes every list as <ol> and marks bullets only with data-list plus editor CSS. That HTML goes out as the body unchanged (Quill's getSemanticHTML is not used), so recipients see ordered lists. Lowered to medium: the formatting is wrong but no content or data is lost.
findings.claim: Rich-text bullet lists reach recipients as numbered lists.
findings.evidence: getHtml returns Quill's internal root.innerHTML, and Compose.GetBodyAndContentTypeAsync sends that markup as the HTML body. [Quill 2.0.3 represents all lists using OL containers](https://github.com/slab/quill/blob/v2.0.3/packages/quill/src/formats/list.ts), distinguishing bullets through data-list and editor CSS. MailSendingService sends a TextPart without that stylesheet, so bullet lists retain ordered-list HTML instead of portable UL markup.

members.claim: Sending a rich-text bullet list changes its formatting into a numbered list for recipients.

findings.reason: AddValidation is not registered anywhere under src, so the [Required]/[StringLength]/[RegularExpression] attributes on SendMailRequest are not enforced. The endpoint only checks request.To.Length and address syntax. A request with To:null throws at line 32 (500), and an empty subject or any ContentType value goes through to SMTP.
findings.claim: The validation attributes on SendMailRequest never run; required fields and size limits go unchecked, and a null recipient list causes a server error.
findings.evidence: SendMailRequest declares Required, StringLength, MaxLength and ContentType constraints, but Program.cs never registers AddValidation and the endpoint manually checks only recipient count and address syntax. [ASP.NET Core requires AddValidation to activate these attributes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/aspnet/core/release-notes/aspnetcore-10.0#enable-built-in-validation-support-for-minimal-apis). A request with valid recipients and an empty subject reaches SMTP; `To: null` fails at request.To.Length, and a null recipient fails at email.Trim().

members.claim: Inactive request validation lets callers bypass required fields and size limits, while null recipients cause server errors.

findings.reason: client.GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) runs before the ?? fallback. MailKit throws NotSupportedException when neither extension is available instead of returning null, so the fallback is skipped. The outer catch only logs a warning, and SendMailAsync still reports success without saving a copy.
findings.claim: On IMAP servers without SPECIAL-USE or XLIST, the fallback to a folder named "Sent" never runs, so sent mail is not saved.
findings.evidence: AppendToSentFolderAsync calls GetFolder(SpecialFolder.Sent) before its null-coalescing folder-name lookup. [MailKit 4.15.1 throws NotSupportedException when neither extension is supported](https://github.com/jstedfast/MailKit/blob/4.15.1/MailKit/Net/Imap/ImapClient.cs#L2159-L2165), even if an ordinary Sent folder exists. The outer catch logs the exception and returns without appending; SendMailAsync subsequently reports success.

members.claim: The Sent-folder fallback never runs on servers without SPECIAL-USE or XLIST, so successfully sent messages lose their saved copy.

The outer catch logs the exception and returns without appending; SendMailAsync subsequently reports success.

findings.reason: LogInformation logs mailbox.EmailAddress and string.Join of request.To. appsettings.json sets the default level to Information, so this is written on every send. It is a privacy and hygiene issue, so it stays low.
findings.claim: Each successful send writes the sender and recipient addresses to Information-level logs and telemetry.
findings.evidence: LogInformation records mailbox.EmailAddress and string.Join(", ", request.To). The default log level is Information, and ServiceDefaults enables formatted OpenTelemetry logging with export when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT is configured. This duplicates personal mail metadata outside the mailbox access controls.

findings.reason: The fixture removes IMailSendingService and registers an NSubstitute substitute. The CC/BCC test matches Arg.Any<SendMailRequest>, and the 404 test makes the substitute throw. MailSendingService itself, including its owner filter, recipient handling and Sent-folder logic, is never run. This is a test-coverage gap, so it stays low.
findings.claim: The new tests replace the whole sending service, so delivery, the mailbox-ownership check and Sent-folder handling are untested.
findings.evidence: The fixture removes IMailSendingService and installs a substitute returning a fixed message ID. The invalid-mailbox test configures that substitute to throw for every request, while the CC/BCC assertion accepts any SendMailRequest. No test exercises MailSendingService, so removing its owner filter, dropping recipients, or breaking SMTP/Sent handling would leave these tests passing.
